To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cholinergic inter-neurons and indirect pathway medium spin neurons have opposing roles in regulating corticostriatal plasticity.
Chl Dd2R and iMSN Drd2R have opposing effects on corticostriatal LTD induction.
D2Rs expressed on cholinergic neurons and indirect pathway MSNs are required for the induction of corticostriatal LTD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular basis of striatal plasticity, and how this relates to the pathophysiology of basal ganglia disorders such as Parkinson’s disease (PD) and Huntington’s disease (HD).
the mechanisms of striatal dopamine (DA) regulation of corticostriatal synaptic plasticity.
the role of dopamine in the regulation of striatal function.

Chl D1Rs and D2Rs are required for LTD induction, and that iMSN D2R are also required, but only in iMSNs.

Chl D1Rs and Chl D2R have a strong modulatory role in eCB mediated LTD induction in MSNS, with iMSN Drd2Rs having a weak iMSN specific modulatory effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
D2Rs on cholinergic neurons play an essential role in eCB mobilization and LTD induction in MSN synapses, while D2Rs on indirect pathway MSNs play a weaker, indirect role.
D2Rs on Chls and iMSNs have distinct roles in eCB-mediated LTD induction in the striatum.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Chl D1R/D5R activation is sufficient for eCB mobilisation and that Chl D5Rs are required for the full expression of LTD.
D2Rs on Chls, not iMSNs, are required for LTD induction in both direct and indirect pathway MSNs.
the D2R mediated control of LTD induction is not limited to a single cell type.
